Description: implicit — interpolate-hcl drops the layer on Native before android-v13.7.1
prompt: One style JSON, shared between our web app (MapLibre GL JS) and our Android app (MapLibre Native, org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk 13.6.1). On Android this layer never draws, while every other layer in the style is fine and there is no crash: `{"id": "density", "type": "fill", "source": "tracts", "source-layer": "tracts", "paint": {"fill-color": ["interpolate-hcl", ["linear"], ["get", "density"], 0, "#f7fbff", 5000, "#08306b"]}}`. The same style is correct in the browser. Where do I look?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
**What you’re seeing** - The layer is **silently dropped** – no crash, no error dialog, the map just shows everything else. - The style uses the **`interpolate-hcl`** expression, which is **not supported in Android 13.6.1**. Support for `interpolate-hcl` (and `interpolate-lab`) was added in **android-v13.7.1** (see the PR #4668 in the Android changelog). When a paint value contains an expression the current Native release cannot parse, the whole layer is removed and the only clue is a log line like: ``` [ParseStyle] value must be a string ``` (You’ll see this if you enable verbose logging.) So the place to look is **the Android logcat output** while the style is being loaded. --- ## Step-by-step checklist | Step | What to do | What you’ll see if the problem is `interpolate-hcl` | |------|------------|------------------------------------------------------| | 1️⃣ | Turn on MapLibre’s debug logging. | ```java MapLibre.getInstance(context).setLogLevel(MapLibre.LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG);``` | | 2️⃣ | Run the app and watch Logcat for lines that contain `ParseStyle` or `value must be a string`. | You’ll get something like:
`[ParseStyle] value must be a string – property fill-color in layer density` | | 3️⃣ | Verify the offending expression is `interpolate-hcl`. | The log will reference the exact expression token. | | 4️⃣ | Check the SDK version you are using. | `android-v13.6.1` (the version you reported) **does not contain** the `interpolate-hcl` implementation. | | 5️⃣ | Decide how to fix it (upgrade or fallback). | See the two options below. | --- ## Fix options ### 1️⃣ Upgrade the SDK (recommended) `interpolate-hcl` landed in **android-v13.7.1** (released 2026-09-xx). Update your Gradle dependency: ```gradle implementation 'org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk:13.7.1' // or newer ``` Re-build and run – the `density` fill layer will render exactly as it does in the browser. ### 2️⃣ Keep the current SDK and replace the expression If you cannot upgrade (e.g., you’re locked to 13.6.1 for other reasons), rewrite the paint value with a plain `interpolate` that approximates the HCL ramp by adding intermediate stops. The visual difference is usually minor for a two-stop ramp. ```json { "id": "density", "type": "fill", "source": "tracts", "source-layer": "tracts", "paint": { "fill-color": [ "interpolate", ["linear"], ["get", "density"], 0, "#f7fbff", 1250, "#d0e1f5", 2500, "#a6cde0", 3750, "#73b3d8", 5000, "#08306b" ] } } ``` *Pick the intermediate colors you like; you can generate an HCL ramp offline (e.g., with a small script) and copy the stops into the style.* --- ## Where to look in the code / docs | Resource | Why it helps | |----------|--------------| | **Android CHANGELOG** (`platform/android/CHANGELOG.md`) | Shows the version that introduced `interpolate-hcl` (v13.7.1). | | **MapLibre Android API – `Expression`** (`org.maplibre.android.style.expressions.Expression`) | No typed builder for `interpolate-hcl`; you must use `Expression.raw()` or JSON. | | **Logcat** (filter `MapLibre` or `ParseStyle`) | The only runtime hint that a layer was dropped because of an unsupported expression. | | **GitHub issue #4668** | PR that added the expressions – useful if you need to back-port the code. | | **Your app’s `build.gradle`** | Verify the exact SDK version you are compiling against. | --- ## Quick “sanity-check” snippet Add this once (e.g., in your `Application` class) to see the exact style-parsing errors in Logcat: ```kotlin import org.maplibre.android.log.Logger import org.maplibre.android.log.LoggerInterface class MyLogger : LoggerInterface { override fun v(tag: String?, msg: String?) = Logger.v(tag, msg) override fun d(tag: String?, msg: String?) = Logger.d(tag, msg) override fun i(tag: String?, msg: String?) = Logger.i(tag, msg) override fun w(tag: String?, msg: String?) = Logger.w(tag, msg) override fun e(tag: String?, msg: String?) = Logger.e(tag, msg) } fun enableDebugLogging(context: Context) { MapLibre.getInstance(context).setLogLevel(Logger.LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG) Logger.setLogger(MyLogger()) } ``` Run the app, open the style, and you’ll see the exact line that caused the layer to be omitted. --- ### TL;DR - **`interpolate-hcl` is not supported in Android 13.6.1** → the `density` layer is dropped. - **Check Logcat** for a `[ParseStyle] value must be a string` message. - **Fix**: upgrade to **android-v13.7.1+** *or* replace the expression with a regular `interpolate` ramp. Once you do either, the layer will appear just like it does in your MapLibre GL JS web app. Happy mapping!

Description: explicit — color-relief exists on MapLibre Native
prompt: Android, MapLibre Native (Kotlin). I have Terrarium-encoded DEM tiles and I want elevation-banded color under my vector layers — green lowlands through brown to white peaks, with the breakpoints in the style so our cartographer can tune them. Can I do that in a MapLibre Android app, or do I have to pre-render colored raster tiles and ship those instead?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
## TL;DR  

**Yes – you can colour-code a Terrarium-encoded DEM on-the-fly in a MapLibre Android app** by using the built-in **`color-relief`** layer (available since **android-v13.0.0**).  
All you need is a **`raster-dem`** source that points at your Terrarium tiles and a `ColorReliefLayer` whose `color-relief-color` paint uses an `["interpolate", …, ["elevation"], …]` expression.  

If you are on a version **earlier than v13.0.0** or you discover that the Terrarium encoding is not being recognised, the fallback is to **pre-render coloured raster tiles** (or convert the DEM to the Mapbox Terrain-RGB format).  

Below is a step-by-step guide, Kotlin snippets, and the gotchas you’ll hit.

---

## 1. What the feature actually is

| Feature | GL JS | MapLibre Native (Android) | First release that ships it |
|---------|------|---------------------------|-----------------------------|
| `color-relief` layer (elevation-banded colour) | ✅ (since 5.6.0) | ✅ (since android-v13.0.0) | 13.0.0 |
| `raster-dem` source that reads Terrarium-encoded tiles | ✅ (`encoding:"terrarium"`) | ✅ (Terrarium support added in the same 13.0.0 release) | 13.0.0 |

> **Bottom line:** As long as you are on **android-v13.0.0** (or newer) you can do exactly what you described – no need to pre-render coloured rasters.

---

## 2. Minimal style JSON (what you would ship to the app)

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "sources": {
    "dem": {
      "type": "raster-dem",
      "url": "https://example.com/tiles/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
      "tileSize": 256,
      "encoding": "terrarium"          // <-- tells the renderer how to decode the DEM
    },
    "vector": {
      "type": "vector",
      "url": "https://example.com/tiles/vector/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf"
    }
  },

  "layers": [
    {
      "id": "color-relief",
      "type": "color-relief",
      "source": "dem",
      "paint": {
        "color-relief-color": [
          "interpolate",
          ["linear"],
          ["elevation"],
          0,   "#2e8b57",   // lowland green
          1500,"#8b5a2b",   // mid-range brown
          3000,"#ffffff"    // peaks white
        ]
      }
    },

    // your normal vector layers go *after* the colour-relief layer
    {
      "id": "roads",
      "type": "line",
      "source": "vector",
      "source-layer": "road",
      "paint": { "line-color": "#000" }
    }
  ]
}
```

*The `color-relief` layer sits **below** the vector layers you want to shade, but **above** any background or fill layers that should stay visible.*

---

## 3. Loading the style in Kotlin

```kotlin
import org.maplibre.android.maps.Style
import org.maplibre.android.maps.MapView
import org.maplibre.android.style.layers.ColorReliefLayer
import org.maplibre.android.style.layers.PropertyFactory
import org.maplibre.android.style.expressions.Expression

// 1️⃣  Create the MapView (in your layout or programmatically)
val mapView = findViewById<MapView>(R.id.mapView)

// 2️⃣  When the map is ready, load the style JSON (local asset or remote URL)
mapView.getMapAsync { mapboxMap ->
    mapboxMap.setStyle(
        Style.Builder()
            .fromUri("asset://my_style.json")   // or .fromUrl("https://…/style.json")
    ) { style ->

        // 3️⃣  If you need to tweak the colour ramp at runtime, you can do it here:
        val relief = style.getLayerAs<ColorReliefLayer>("color-relief")
        relief?.setProperties(
            PropertyFactory.colorReliefColor(
                Expression.raw(
                    """["interpolate", ["linear"], ["elevation"],
                       0, "#2e8b57",
                       1500, "#8b5a2b",
                       3000, "#ffffff"]"""
                )
            )
        )
    }
}
```

*All the heavy lifting (decoding Terrarium PNGs, extracting the elevation, applying the colour ramp) is done inside the native renderer.*

---

## 4. What to do if the DEM isn’t being decoded

### 4.1 Verify you are on a recent Native version  

* `android-v13.0.0` (released 2026-03-12) introduced both **Terrarium support** and the **`color-relief`** layer.  
* If you are on an older version (e.g. `android-v13.6.0` or earlier) the renderer will **ignore the `encoding` key** and treat the tiles as plain RGB, which results in a flat map (no elevation).  

**Fix:** bump the MapLibre Android dependency:

```gradle
implementation "org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk:13.0.0"
```

or any newer version (`13.7.1` is the latest as of 2026-10-15).

### 4.2 The tiles still look flat?  

*Double-check the URL pattern* – the renderer only recognises `http(s)://` URLs.  
If you are using a custom scheme (`vault://…`) you must serve the tiles through the **`ModuleProvider`** HTTP interceptor (see the “Custom URL schemes” section of the `maplibre-native-gl-js-parity` skill).  

### 4.3 Terrarium not supported (rare edge case)  

If you discover that the native build you are using **does not yet understand `encoding":"terrarium"`** (e.g. a custom-built fork), you have two options:

| Option | What you do |
|--------|-------------|
| **Convert to Mapbox Terrain-RGB** | Use a server-side script (e.g. GDAL `gdal_translate -of PNG -scale 0 65535 0 255`) to produce the standard Terrain-RGB tiles. Then change the source to `"encoding":"mapbox"` (or omit the key – Terrain-RGB is the default). |
| **Pre-render coloured rasters** | Generate a coloured PNG for each tile (e.g. with GDAL `gdaldem color-relief`) and serve those as a normal `raster` source. This works on any Native version but loses the ability to change the colour ramp at runtime. |

---

## 5. Full-featured example (including a UI slider for the cartographer)

```kotlin
class MapActivity : AppCompatActivity() {

    private lateinit var mapView: MapView
    private var style: Style? = null

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        setContentView(R.layout.activity_map)

        mapView = findViewById(R.id.mapView)
        mapView.onCreate(savedInstanceState)

        mapView.getMapAsync { mapboxMap ->
            mapboxMap.setStyle(
                Style.Builder()
                    .fromUri("asset://my_style.json")
            ) { loadedStyle ->
                style = loadedStyle
                // Hook a SeekBar to let the cartographer tweak the middle breakpoint
                findViewById<SeekBar>(R.id.breakpointSeek).setOnSeekBarChangeListener(
                    object : SeekBar.OnSeekBarChangeListener {
                        override fun onProgressChanged(seekBar: SeekBar?, progress: Int, fromUser: Boolean) {
                            updateReliefRamp(progress * 10) // progress 0-300 → elevation 0-3000 m
                        }
                        override fun onStartTrackingTouch(seekBar: SeekBar?) {}
                        override fun onStopTrackingTouch(seekBar: SeekBar?) {}
                    })
            }
        }
    }

    private fun updateReliefRamp(midpointMeters: Int) {
        val relief = style?.getLayerAs<ColorReliefLayer>("color-relief") ?: return
        val expr = Expression.raw(
            """["interpolate", ["linear"], ["elevation"],
               0, "#2e8b57",
               $midpointMeters, "#8b5a2b",
               3000, "#ffffff"]"""
        )
        relief.setProperties(PropertyFactory.colorReliefColor(expr))
    }

    // … lifecycle callbacks (onStart, onStop, …) omitted for brevity
}
```

*The cartographer can now slide the breakpoint between green and brown without rebuilding the app or re-tiling the DEM.*

---

## 6. Quick checklist before you ship

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| **Native version ≥ 13.0.0** | Guarantees `color-relief` and Terrarium support. |
| **`raster-dem` source with `"encoding":"terrarium"`** | Tells the renderer how to decode the PNG DEM. |
| **`color-relief` layer placed below vector layers** | Gives the “elevation-banded colour” effect. |
| **If you use a custom URL scheme** – implement a `ModuleProvider` or `OkHttp` interceptor (see the “Custom URL schemes” skill). |
| **Test on a device with a low-zoom view** – you should see the colour ramp change as you zoom out (the DEM tiles are still read, just at lower resolution). |
| **Optional UI for ramp tweaking** – use `Expression.raw()` to rebuild the ramp on the fly. |

---

## 7. When you *must* pre-render coloured rasters

If you are **stuck on an older Native version** (e.g. `android-v12.x.x`) **or** you need to support **offline tiles bundled in the APK** *and* you cannot upgrade, the only path is to **pre-render the colour-relief raster** (e.g. with `gdaldem color-relief`) and serve it as a normal `raster` source. This loses the ability to change the colour stops at runtime, but works on every Native release.

---

## 8. TL;DR code summary

```kotlin
// 1. Add the raster-dem source (Terrarium)
style.addSource(
    RasterDemSource("dem") {
        url("https://example.com/tiles/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png")
        tileSize(256)
        encoding("terrarium")   // <-- important
    }
)

// 2. Add the colour-relief layer
style.addLayer(
    ColorReliefLayer("relief", "dem").withProperties(
        PropertyFactory.colorReliefColor(
            Expression.raw(
                """["interpolate", ["linear"], ["elevation"],
                   0, "#2e8b57",
                   1500, "#8b5a2b",
                   3000, "#ffffff"]"""
            )
        )
    )
)

// 3. Add your vector layers *after* the relief layer
// (or reorder with style.moveLayer(...))
```

---

### Bottom line

> **You do NOT have to pre-render coloured raster tiles.**  
> With MapLibre Android **v13.0.0+** you can point a `raster-dem` source at your Terrarium-encoded DEM tiles and add a `color-relief` layer that colours the terrain on-the-fly. The cartographer can tune the breakpoints directly in the style (or via a UI control) and the app will render the coloured relief instantly.  

If you are on an older version or run into a Terrarium-decoding bug, upgrade or convert the DEM to Terrain-RGB, or fall back to pre-rendered rasters.

Description: explicit — pmtiles:// is a built-in MapLibre Native scheme
prompt: iOS, Swift, MapLibre Native. Our basemap is one 3 GB `.pmtiles` archive on Cloudflare R2. On the web we register the PMTiles protocol with the `pmtiles` npm package and point the source at `pmtiles://https://...`. What is the iOS equivalent — do I need to stand up a tile server, convert the archive to MBTiles, or write a custom source?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
**Short answer**

You **do not** need a tile server, an MBTiles conversion, or a custom source.  
MapLibre Native for iOS has built-in support for the `pmtiles://` scheme (since **iOS v6.10.0**).  
Just point the vector-tile source in your style (or create it in code) to the URL you already use on the web:

```json
{
  "id": "world",
  "type": "vector",
  "url": "pmtiles://https://<your-cloudflare-r2-bucket>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/world.pmtiles"
}
```

or, in Swift:

```swift
let worldSource = MLNVectorTileSource(
    identifier: "world",
    configurationURLString: "pmtiles://https://<your-cloudflare-r2-bucket>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/world.pmtiles"
)

style?.addSource(worldSource)
```

That’s it – the archive will be streamed directly from Cloudflare R2 and cached by MapLibre’s internal tile cache.

---

## Why this works

| Feature | GL JS | MapLibre Native iOS |
|---------|-------|----------------------|
| `pmtiles://` protocol | Added by the `pmtiles` npm package (`addProtocol`) | Built-in since **ios-v6.10.0** (pull #2882) |
| Remote archive loading | `pmtiles://https://…` works out of the box | Same URL works; the native code resolves the scheme and streams the archive over HTTP/HTTPS |
| Need for a server / conversion | No | No |

The native implementation reads the archive itself; it does **not** require a separate tile-server, nor does it need the archive to be converted to MBTiles.  

> **Note:** The only gotcha is the iOS 17 URL-parsing bug. The `URL(string:)` initializer mangles the double-scheme (`pmtiles://https://…`). Use the `configurationURLString:` initializer (the string version) instead of the `URL` version.

---

## Step-by-step guide for a Swift app

1. **Add the PMTiles archive URL to your style** (JSON or programmatically).  
   *If you keep the style in a file, just edit the source entry as shown above.*  

2. **Load the style in your `MLNMapView`.**  
   ```swift
   mapView.styleURL = URL(string: "https://example.com/your-style.json")!
   ```

3. **If you prefer to add the source in code (e.g. you want to set a different source for different zoom levels):**
   ```swift
   // 1️⃣ Make sure the map’s style is loaded
   mapView.style?.let { style in
       // 2️⃣ Create the PMTiles source
       let pmtilesSource = MLNVectorTileSource(
           identifier: "world",
           configurationURLString: "pmtiles://https://<your-r2-bucket>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/world.pmtiles"
       )
       
       // 3️⃣ Add the source to the style
       style.addSource(pmtilesSource)
       
       // 4️⃣ Add a layer that uses the source (example: a fill layer)
       let fillLayer = MLNFillStyleLayer(identifier: "land", source: pmtilesSource)
       fillLayer.sourceLayerIdentifier = "land"          // <-- name of the source-layer inside the PMTiles
       fillLayer.fillColor = NSExpression(forConstantValue: UIColor.systemGreen)
       style.addLayer(fillLayer)
   }
   ```

4. **Network configuration (optional).**  
   MapLibre builds its `URLSession` from `MLNNetworkConfiguration.sharedManager.sessionConfiguration`.  
   If you need to add custom headers, a proxy, or a certificate pinning, modify that configuration **before** the first `MLNMapView` is created:

   ```swift
   let config = MLNNetworkConfiguration.sharedManager.sessionConfiguration
   config.httpAdditionalHeaders = ["Authorization": "Bearer <your-token>"]
   // any other URLSession tweaks …
   ```

5. **Caching** – MapLibre automatically caches fetched tiles (both vector tiles and the PMTiles archive itself) in its on-disk cache. No extra code is required.

---

## Common pitfalls & how to avoid them

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| **No tiles appear, but no error** | The source URL was built with `URL(string:)` → iOS 17 strips the second scheme (`pmtiles://https://…`). | Use `configurationURLString:` (the string-based initializer) as shown above. |
| **Tiles load slowly / repeatedly** | The default cache size is small on a fresh install. | Increase the cache size via `MLNSettings.tileCacheSize` (in MB) **before** creating the map view: `MLNSettings.tileCacheSize = 1024` (1 GB). |
| **HTTPS certificate error** | Cloudflare R2 uses a custom TLS configuration that the default `URLSession` does not trust (rare). | Add the appropriate `URLSessionDelegate` to the `sessionConfiguration` or pin the certificate. |
| **Archive is > 2 GB and you get a “file too large” error** | On iOS < 15 the underlying file-source had a 2 GB limit. | Use iOS 15+ (the current minimum for MapLibre Native) – the limit was lifted in the native code after v6.10.0. |
| **You see “[ParseStyle]: value must be a string”** | The style contains an expression (`interpolate-hcl` / `interpolate-lab`) that the installed native version does not support. | Upgrade to **ios-v7.0.0** (or later) or replace the expression with a plain `interpolate` ramp. |

---

## When you *do* need a custom source

Only consider a custom source if you need **one of the following** that the built-in PMTiles support cannot provide:

| Need | Native solution |
|------|-----------------|
| **On-the-fly reprojection** (e.g., from WebMercator to another projection) | Write a `CustomVectorSource` (Android) – not available on iOS yet. |
| **Per-tile authentication that cannot be expressed via HTTP headers** | Implement a `URLProtocol` subclass that intercepts `pmtiles://` requests and injects the auth token. |
